Engineering Notes

The details documentation summaries usually skip.

Small operational traps worth preserving because they are usually learned after something fails.

Kubernetes

ConfigMap subPath mounts do not refresh

Normal projected ConfigMap files can update eventually; a subPath mount does not receive those automatic updates.

Kubernetes

Readiness and liveness answer different questions

Readiness decides traffic eligibility. Liveness decides whether the container should be restarted.

Docker

Container IPs are implementation detail

User-defined Docker networks provide DNS-based names. Hard-coded container IPs turn normal replacement into an outage.

Linux Security

Every listening port needs an owner

Service inventory comes before firewall confidence. Know what is listening and why.

Networking

Troubleshooting needs an order

DNS → route → transport → TLS → proxy → backend → disk is a more useful sequence than random command roulette.

Ansible

Rollback can still be failure

A successful rescue path can leave a play green unless the deployment failure is deliberately re-raised.

AWS

NACLs are stateless

Security Groups track connection state; NACL design must account for both directions and ephemeral return traffic.

AWS

CloudTrail and CloudWatch are different evidence

CloudTrail answers who called what AWS API; CloudWatch answers operational questions from metrics, logs and alarms.
